memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "But if he has a reddish-white sore on his bald head or forehead, it is a defiling disease breaking out on his head or forehead. The priest is to examine him, and if the swollen sore on his head or forehead is reddish-white like a defiling skin disease, the man is diseased and is unclean. The priest shall pronounce him unclean because of the sore on his head." - Lev 13:42-44 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Baldness itself was clean. But if a genuine sore appeared there, it was examined by exactly the same standard as anywhere else on the body. No exemption. No special category.

God's standards do not bend for anyone.

We have a strong instinct to make exceptions — usually for ourselves and the people we like. We excuse in a friend what we would condemn in a stranger. We understand our own harsh words because we know what kind of week we have had. We give ourselves the benefit of a doubt we rarely extend to others.

Scripture is firm here. God does not show favouritism (Rom 2:11). Peter learned this in Cornelius's house and said it aloud: I now realise how true it is that God does not show favouritism (Acts 10:34). And James warns the church directly against treating the rich man better than the poor one (Jas 2:1-4).

There is real comfort in this alongside the challenge. If God does not play favourites, then no one has an inside track that you lack. Your background, your income, your family name, your church position — none of it buys you standing, and none of it excludes you either.

The same standard, the same grace, for all.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where do you apply a different standard to yourself than to others?
2. Do you ever feel God favours certain people over you?
3. How would treating everyone impartially change your relationships this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You show no favouritism, and that Your grace is offered on the same terms to everyone. Root out the double standards in me and give me a fair heart. Amen.
